title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Lena Ortiz
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended process and artifacts for enterprise customer onboarding, integration guidance, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, and recurring health checks / QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Support, and SRE partners. Use this playbook as the canonical checklist for a new enterprise starting production traffic, and as the reference during QBRs and postmortems.

Scope

- New enterprise onboarding into Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments
- Cross-functional responsibilities: Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support (Tier 1–3), SRE/Platform, and Product
- Includes integration steps, acceptance criteria, escalation flows, and QBR template

Owners and primary contacts

- CS Owner: Lena Ortiz (author) — cs-leads@redwoodinference.com
- SE Lead: Marcus Li — solutions@redwoodinference.com
- Support Triage: support@redwoodinference.com (primary mailbox)
- SRE Oncall: #sre-oncall (Slack) / page: oncall.redwoodinference.com
- Escalation Pager: +1-555-0110 (for Severity 1 after CS notification)

Onboarding checklist (milestone-driven)

1) Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Share onboarding charter and success criteria.
   - Confirm deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
   - Assign primary CS/SE contacts and technical owners.

2) Integration (Week 0–2)
   - Provide API keys and environment details (staging / prod).
   - Deliver Quickstart: token-based curl example and SDK sample.
   - Validate connectivity: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health (expect 200 + version).

3) Load & Performance Baseline (Week 2–4)
   - Run baseline tests with customer workload; capture P50/P95/P99 latencies and throughput.
   - Configure quotas and rate limits; propose reserved capacity if needed.

4) Quality Acceptance (Week 2–6)
   - Run acceptance prompt set (shared by CS) and compare against golden baseline.
   - If regression detected, open regression ticket and schedule model tuning/onboarding with Applied ML.

5) Go‑Live (Week 4–8)
   - Finalize DNS, webhooks, and traffic routing policy.
   - Confirm monitoring dashboards and alerting subscriptions.
   - Execute gradual ramp (canary + linear ramp) per rollout policy in eng-platform docs.

Integration guide (API & webhook fundamentals)

- API authentication: Use a project-scoped API key; rotate keys via Console > Security > API Keys.
- Typical request example (curl):

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.3","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

- Webhook setup (for async workflows):
  1. Create secure endpoint (HTTPS, TLS 1.2+).
  2. Add endpoint in Console > Integrations > Webhooks, include shared secret.
  3. Validate by sending test payload from Console.

- Recommended retry/backoff: implement exponential backoff (initial 500ms, factor 2, max 16s) for 429/5xx responses.
- Response schema: responses contain top-level id, model, tokens_consumed, and result. See sample JSON in Appendix.

Acceptance & SLA targets for onboarding (recommended)

| Metric | Acceptance threshold | Operational SLO (post-go-live) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 5xx error rate | < 0.1% during load test | < 0.5% monthly |
| 429 rate (per-client) | < 1% at expected throughput | < 2% monthly |
| P95 latency (generation, small prompts) | < 450 ms | P95 < 600 ms |
| P99 latency | < 900 ms | P99 < 1200 ms |
| Availability (platform control plane) | 99.9% during onboarding window | 99.9% monthly |

Escalation playbook (tiered severity)

Severity definitions
1. Sev 1 (Critical) — platform-wide outage or customer production completely down, revenue-impacting.
2. Sev 2 (High) — partial outage affecting critical features or significant degradation for a single or small set of customers.
3. Sev 3 (Medium) — functional impact with workaround; intermittent errors.
4. Sev 4 (Low) — informational or non-urgent configuration requests.

Escalation flow (summary)

1) Customer reports issue to support@redwoodinference.com or CS rep. Triage within 15 minutes.
2) Assign severity based on impact and confirm with customer.
3) For Sev 1:
   - Immediately notify SRE oncall: #sre-oncall and call escalation pager if no ack in 5 minutes.
   - CS notifies customer success exec and schedules bridge (Zoom) within 15 minutes.
   - Create incident in Incident Manager and follow incident runbook (link in related_pages).
4) For Sev 2:
   - Triage with Support + SE; escalate to Engineering lead if unresolved after 1 hour.
5) For Sev 3/4:
   - Document in support ticket and schedule remediation in next sprint or patch release as appropriate.

Escalation contacts (primary)

- Support Triage (24/7): support@redwoodinference.com
- SRE Oncall: #sre-oncall (Slack) / pager: +1-555-0110
- CS Escalation: cs-leads@redwoodinference.com
- Product Eng Escalation (weekday): eng-leads@redwoodinference.com

Known issues & recommended workarounds (common categories)

1) Increased latency on long prompt chains
   - Symptoms: P95/P99 elevated when using prompts with large context windows.
   - Workaround: Reduce prompt context, enable prefix KV cache for repeated system prompt, or use shorter chunking. Consider model variant with optimized long context.

2) Sporadic 429s under bursty traffic
   - Symptoms: Short bursts of 429s for individual API keys.
   - Workaround: Implement client-side backoff with jitter; request quota increase or enable burst capacity for Dedicated customers.

3) Model output regressions after model switch
   - Symptoms: Quality drop for specific prompts following a model variant upgrade.
   - Workaround: Rollback to pinned model version, open regression ticket with Applied ML, and run evaluation harness with customer prompt-set.

4) Webhook delivery failures due to TLS issues
   - Symptoms: 401/502 from webhook delivery logs.
   - Workaround: Validate TLS certificate chain and supported ciphers; test endpoint with curl --http2 and check firewall egress rules.

Support process and SLAs

- Response targets (by severity):
  - Sev 1: initial response 15 minutes, continuous updates every 15 minutes until mitigated.
  - Sev 2: initial response 1 hour, updates every 2 hours until resolved.
  - Sev 3: initial response 4 business hours.
  - Sev 4: response within 2 business days.

- Ticket ownership: Support owns triage; CS owns customer communications for enterprise accounts; Engineering owns code-level fixes and root cause analysis.

Health checks, dashboards, and QBR template

Recommended dashboards (Console / Grafana):
- API: request rate, 4xx/5xx rates, 429 rate per API key, P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens per request distribution.
- Serving runtime: GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, queue length.
- Billing/usage: tokens consumed by route, cost per token, month-to-date usage vs committed.

Weekly health check checklist (CS & SE)
- Confirm connectivity and average latency against SLOs.
- Review error spikes and open tickets.
- Check recent deployment rollouts and any fallbacks used.
- Validate webhook delivery rates and backoff behavior.

QBR agenda (template)

1) Executive summary: adoption, business impact, and topline metrics (5–10 mins)
2) Operational health: latency, errors, incidents since last QBR (15 mins)
3) Usage and cost: consumption trends and cost optimization recommendations (10 mins)
4) Product roadmap & upcoming model changes (10 mins)
5) Action items & next steps: ownership and timelines (5 mins)

Appendix (links, sample commands, artifacts)
